evals.prompt: set up a new repo for my software interview prep assistant: it should quiz me on algorithms and system design, run mock interviews, and track what I keep getting wrong
evals.expected_output: An assistant-profile repo, Python by default, with a tutor recipe (learner model, review and mock skills, rubrics, FSRS scheduling) and a 100% strict setup score.
expectations: Chooses the assistant profile and the tutor recipe from references/assistant-recipes.md
Asks at most one round of at most three questions, or states its defaults
Runs scaffold.sh with --profile assistant, then the stack generator for the chosen stack
Plans a learner model under private/, review and mock skills, binary rubrics shared by feedback and judge, and FSRS scheduling
Adds eval cases that check the tutor withholds the solution before an attempt and refrains on a quick factual question
Keeps personal data out of git: private/ is ignored and eval cases are synthetic
Routes models through config/models.yaml with the local route first and never proposes xAI or Grok
Runs check-setup.sh --profile assistant --strict and scripts/check.sh and shows both outputs before reporting done

evals.prompt: bootstrap a new CLI tool that converts markdown task files to calendar events
evals.expected_output: A tool-profile TypeScript repo with CHANGELOG, LICENSE, cli-design in the Agentfile, a wired gate, and a 100% strict score.
expectations: Checks for prior art before building and records a verdict in docs/VISION.md
Chooses the tool profile and TypeScript, and records the stack in an ADR
Runs the stack generator and adds lint, typecheck, and test scripts that scripts/check.sh runs
Adds one smoke test so the gate proves something on day one
Fills every FILL: marker or names the ones the user must fill
Shows check-setup.sh --profile tool --strict at 100% and a green scripts/check.sh

evals.prompt: I want to start a private side project: an offline log of my garden plants with photos, to know when to water. Nobody should ever see my photos.
evals.expected_output: A side-project repo with a privacy doc, an ignored private/ folder, synthetic fixtures, VISION with a success metric and dated kill criteria.
expectations: Chooses the side-project profile and a private repo
Writes docs/privacy.md and keeps the user's photos under private/ or outside the repo, never in tests or commits
Writes VISION with a measurable success metric and a dated kill criterion
Uses only synthetic fixtures in tests
Does not push or create a remote unless the user asked

evals.prompt: new project: a log analyzer that has to chew through 50 GB of files fast on my laptop and ship as a single binary
evals.expected_output: A tool-profile repo on the Rust stack with cargo fmt, clippy, and tests wired into the gate.
expectations: Picks Rust because of the heavy-app row in references/stacks.md (speed, big files, single binary)
Runs cargo init and relies on scripts/check.sh to run cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, and cargo test
Records the stack choice and its reason in an ADR

evals.prompt: my existing repo has no AGENTS.md, can you add one?
evals.expected_output: Does not scaffold a new project; points to the agent guide baseline for an existing repo instead.
expectations: Recognizes this is an existing repo, not a new project
Does not run scaffold.sh over the existing repo
Routes to the agent-guide baseline (docs/agent-guide-baseline.md) or agentfile-init as appropriate

evals.prompt: quickly hack a throwaway script to test whether this API returns pagination cursors
evals.expected_output: Does not use this skill; a throwaway spike belongs to prototype or a plain script.
expectations: Does not create a full project scaffold for a throwaway question
Suggests the prototype skill or a single script
Does not run scaffold.sh or check-setup.sh

evals.prompt: start a new project for a habit tracker web app; it must have full observability, metrics, vision, user stories, a one-line setup, e2e tests, a way to keep getting faster, tasks, one checkup command, and fast but full tests
evals.expected_output: A tool-profile repo where check-setup.sh reports every required area (vision, metrics, observability, user-stories, setup, e2e, self-improving, tasks) passing, and the one-line setup and full gate actually run green.
expectations: Runs check-setup.sh and shows its areas line listing vision, metrics, observability, user-stories, setup, e2e, self-improving, tasks, checkup, and caching
Runs scripts/setup.sh and shows it ending with 'doctor: all checks passed'
Writes the first real user story with its metric and an e2e test per case, listed in docs/user-stories.md so scripts/check-docs.sh passes
Fills the metrics table in docs/observability.md with goal, pivot, and command for each metric, using (stub) for missing data
Runs the full scripts/check.sh (with e2e) and then scripts/metrics.sh to show the timed steps
Leaves RECURRING.md with the weekly speed review and checkup instead of deleting them
Runs scripts/check.sh twice and shows the second run skipping steps as cached, then shows a file change making every step run again

evals.prompt: run the monthly requirements audit on this existing repo; it keeps VISION.md at the root and has no runtime logs because it is a spec repo
evals.expected_output: Runs audit-due.sh, maps the area to the repo's own files in .agents/requirements.yaml, waives only with a concrete reason, keeps one P0 task listing every gap, and records the run.
expectations: Runs scripts/audit-due.sh first and stops when it prints not due
Adds map.vision: VISION.md instead of moving the file, after checking VISION.md really has a success metric and kill criteria
Waives an area only with a concrete reason a reviewer would accept, never 'too much work'
Updates the single P0 task meet-new-project-requirements instead of filing a duplicate
Proposes a change to the new-project requirement when the same waiver appears in two or more repos
Runs audit-due.sh --record at the end

evals.prompt: bring this existing npm-workspace tool repo (root VISION.md, a doctor command, git-native task queue) to 100% on check-setup.sh --profile tool, mapping or waiving areas where its own files already meet them
evals.expected_output: Reaches 100% with map lines that each name existing files (VISION.md, the doctor source file, the docs-contract check) and a comment saying why, adds the missing pieces (metrics table, setup script, e2e per story, content-free logs, cached gate, checkup, learnings, ADRs) instead of waiving them, and adds each map line in the PR that makes it true.
expectations: Maps the health check to the file that implements the doctor command, not to the command name
Checks before mapping that VISION.md has a dated numeric goal, a pivot, and dated kill criteria, and adds them when missing
Builds the cached gate so a change to any file a test reads re-runs that test, and proves it by editing a file and showing the cache miss
Waives nothing for effort; every area ends met or mapped with a reason
Runs check-setup.sh on main after the last merge for the final score

evals.prompt: scaffold a new CLI tool repo and fill in its first two user stories, metrics, and event log
evals.expected_output: Each story's metric is an outcome rate users feel (for example the share of failed events for that story), with the e2e test count kept only as a guard; each e2e file names its story id; the event writer allow-lists string fields and tests turn the log off; metrics pin their exact query and show (stub) when a source would answer 0 for something missing; the CHANGELOG is set up to be generated at release.
expectations: Writes no story metric that is only a count of passing tests
Each tests/e2e/us-NN file contains its US-NN id and scripts/check-docs.sh passes
The event writer rejects a string field that could hold free text, and a test asserts the log is off during tests
A metric whose source can answer 0 for a missing thing checks that the thing exists and shows (stub) otherwise
Every doctor FAIL line names its fix
check-setup.sh --profile tool reaches 100% on the scaffold

evals.prompt: the new-project rules changed; make sure my existing tool repo still matches them
evals.expected_output: Checks each changed rule by intent against the repo (not only the scorer), finds stories whose metric is a passing-test count, replaces them with outcome metrics that have a pinned query, goal, pivot, and a (stub) path, keeps the test counts as Guard lines, and turns the rule into a docs check that fails on a test-count metric.
expectations: Lists every changed rule with PASS or FAIL and evidence before editing
Takes baselines for new outcome metrics from a real source (code search, labelled issues, the event log) and pins the exact query
Creates a missing label before counting it, and prints (stub) when the label is missing
Adds a check (with a red-then-green test) so a story metric cannot fall back to a test count
Reports the scorer at 100% on main after the merge

evals.prompt: prove my repo's gate cache keys list every file a step reads
evals.expected_output: A red-then-green test that edits one tracked file and one untracked file and reruns the SAME command, plus a check that a test reading a changed file by repo path is selected by the affected-test logic.
expectations: Reruns the same command after the edit; a test that changes the command proves nothing because the command is part of the key
Covers an edit to an untracked file's content, not only a new untracked file
Checks that affected-test selection picks a test that reads the changed file by repo path (for example a root AGENTS.md)
Shows the new test failing before the fix and passing after

evals.prompt: new assistant repo for career help; my machine has a global core.hooksPath from dotfiles and the app handles employer data
evals.expected_output: The scaffold keeps working git hooks despite the global hooksPath (repo-local hooks/pre-commit and hooks/pre-push that the global hook delegates to), skill frontmatter that parses as YAML, and a privacy doc that lists every data exit including the agent transcript, each with a guard and a canary test.
expectations: Ships hooks/pre-commit and hooks/pre-push so secret and docs checks run when lefthook install is skipped
Every skills/*/SKILL.md description parses as YAML (no bare ': ' in the value)
docs/privacy.md lists data exits including the agent transcript (stdout), each with a guard and a test
Uses an allowlist .gitignore and adds the hooks folder to it

evals.prompt: my assistant repo's README grew a long command list and check-setup now fails the setup check
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the failing check's label, sees that the docs/README.md link must appear in the first 60 lines of the README, adds a docs-map line near the top instead of trimming useful content, and reruns check-setup to 100%.
expectations: Reads the check label or script to learn the 60-line docs-link rule
Keeps the README content and adds the docs map link near the top
Reruns check-setup and shows 100%

evals.prompt: evolve my existing Rust + Python cash-forecast repo into a personal assistant and follow all my app standards
evals.expected_output: The agent scores the repo with check-setup.sh --profile assistant first (baseline), scaffolds the missing files into the non-empty repo without overwriting, adds an engine step for the subfolder Cargo.toml, names pytest story tests tests/e2e/test_usNN_*.py and lists them in docs/user-stories.md, keeps scripts/setup.sh as the first line of the README's first code block, and reruns check-setup --strict to 100%.
expectations: Takes the check-setup baseline before editing
Scaffolds into the existing repo and keeps existing files
Adds a gate step for the subfolder Cargo.toml
Story tests named test_usNN are listed and checked by check-docs
Shows check-setup --strict at 100%

evals.prompt: my Python finance assistant prints a long strategy document; users need to plan ahead and switch between views
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps the Python logic, adds a local JSON API, and builds the UI as a TypeScript web app (React + Vite) with one view per section and a planning view; it records the choice in an ADR and adds the web lint, typecheck, test and build to scripts/check.sh and CI.
expectations: UI is TypeScript, not Python templates or a notes app
Logic stays in the existing language behind a JSON API
An ADR records the TypeScript-for-multi-view-UI rule
The gate and CI build, lint, typecheck and test the web app

evals.prompt: new project: a things-to-do assistant for a couple, with week, month, year views and voting from phones
evals.expected_output: The agent picks the assistant profile but the TypeScript stack (Vite + React + Hono) because the UI has several views, scaffolds, checks that CLAUDE.md is a relative symlink to AGENTS.md and that .copier-answers.yml holds no local path or private name before the first push, and records the stack choice in an ADR.
expectations: Chooses TypeScript because the UI has more than one view
CLAUDE.md is a symlink to AGENTS.md, not an absolute path
No local home path or owner name is pushed in .copier-answers.yml
Writes an ADR for the stack

evals.prompt: new project: a personal assistant that tracks my reading; I want to just run one command and have it work
evals.expected_output: The scaffold starts the app with one command: `<name>` with no arguments in the shell and `/<name>` in an agent (commands/<name>.md declared in Agentfile.yaml). It uses sane defaults from one table, and `<name> config` / `config set` show and change them. check-setup's [start] check passes.
expectations: commands/<name>.md exists and Agentfile.yaml declares commands
The README quickstart names the one-command start and `config set`
check-setup.sh reports PASS for the [start] area
